sections.title: The group wr
paragraphs: The letters wr make one sound. You hear this sound in (wrist) /rɪst/, the joint between the arm and the hand. The group has only one sound. The first letter stays completely quiet.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Curl your tongue tip slightly back toward the roof of your mouth. Do not let your tongue touch the roof. Round your lips gently. Voice this sound so your vocal cords shake. Put your hand on your throat to feel the shaking.

sections.title: When to use it
paragraphs: This group appears at the beginning of words before a vowel. You hear it at the start of (write) /raɪt/. You also hear this sound in the word (wrong) /rɒŋ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not try to say both written letters. Many learners try to pronounce the first consonant as an extra sound. Start right away with the single sound of the second consonant.
